- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 3–8% in subsequent days to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is falling, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% to capture mean reversion.
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above true outcome, apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period to account for delayed reaction.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is >10% above 18-day moving average, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with momentum.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.2–0.5) and model is erratic, apply smoothing: average 3–5 prior forecasts before projecting next.
